title: Product name: workthread everywhere; the repository and `CONTEXT.md` stay authoritative
"Itinerary Planner" survives only as the title of the moved specification document
This effort is done when every child effort for planner v1 exists as a live effort under `docs/tasks/` with its own map, scope, entry criteria, and `origin_effort: planner-v1`
Every cross-cutting architecture and product decision a child would otherwise have to settle is recorded in `docs/tasks/planner-v1/architecture.md` or in an ADR
No product code, no build files, no CI configuration, no module skeleton
No implementation of any v1 capability
No v2 advisory work (specification sections 7 and 10)
No calendar, billing, team, kanban, chat, plugin marketplace, or autonomous scheduling scope
No release or packaging work
to-spec writes the specification, to-tickets writes `architecture.md` and exactly one ticket
finalize closes the effort on branch `effort/planner-v1`, merged back with `--no-ff` and pushed
The single ticket is a formality: it carries no implementation, it is marked `mode: human` so the router hard-refuses autonomous dispatch, and it exists only to clear the finalizable gate
One document, `docs/tasks/planner-v1/architecture.md`, written by to-tickets through `tw_write_architecture` and reconciled at the close
Child efforts copy the parts they own
The 16 open decisions are grouped into five themed grillings, one grilling per Wayfinder pass; each decision belongs to exactly one group
estimates and time semantics: DEC-1, DEC-13
forecasts, risk, and warnings: DEC-2, DEC-5, DEC-6, DEC-7, DEC-8, DEC-15, DEC-16
service mode and lifecycle: DEC-3, DEC-4, plus the open architecture of section 6.7
data lifecycle: DEC-10, DEC-11, DEC-12, DEC-14, plus the persistence choice
agent interface: DEC-9, plus the MCP surface, the change feed, agent attribution, and notification delivery
One research task on the Java stack before the service-mode decision and the decomposition: MCP server library for Java, keeping the core independent of Spring, JavaFX test...
Build tool and test harness: settled in this effort, not by the scaffolding child, and recorded in the architecture document
The human wants to add requirements on top of the specification before any research or decision grilling starts, so an open-ended grilling task runs first and every other planning task...
Child efforts are separate efforts under `docs/tasks/`, recorded in the map's `## Child efforts` section with scope, dependency position, and entry criteria
Each child effort is created at the close as an accepted follow-up, with `origin_effort: planner-v1` on its map, after a human yes
Child efforts are never tickets and never `blocked_by` edges
`spec-additions` (grilling): the human adds requirements on top of the specification. Blocked by `non-negotiables`
`stack-research` (research): the Java stack. Blocked by `spec-additions`
`decisions-estimates-time` (grilling): DEC-1, DEC-13. Blocked by `spec-additions`
`decisions-forecast-warnings` (grilling): DEC-2, DEC-5, DEC-6, DEC-7, DEC-8, DEC-15, DEC-16. Blocked by `spec-additions`
`decisions-service-mode` (grilling): DEC-3, DEC-4, and section 6.7. Blocked by `spec-additions` and `stack-research`
`decisions-data-lifecycle` (grilling): DEC-10, DEC-11, DEC-12, DEC-14, plus persistence. Blocked by `spec-additions` and `stack-research`
`decisions-agent-interface` (grilling): DEC-9, the MCP surface, the change feed, attribution, and notification delivery. Blocked by `spec-additions` and `stack-research`
`child-efforts` (grilling): the child-effort list. Blocked by every task above
The child-effort list itself is the `child-efforts` task, not an open question
